hints.title: Euclidean Squared Distance Metric
hints.text: The Euclidean distance from the origin (0, 0) is proportional to x^2 + y^2, avoiding square root computations.

hints.title: Partial Selection Order
hints.text: Only the k closest points are required, in any order. Sorting or selection algorithms partition the k smallest distances efficiently.

hints.title: Key-Based Sort or Quickselect
hints.text: Sort points using key lambda p: p[0]**2 + p[1]**2. Slice the first k elements and return them.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: K: number of closest points requested
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Computing full sorted distances takes O(N log N); using Quickselect or a bounded heap of size K can improve this to O(N).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place sorting achieves O(N log N) time with O(1) auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that comparing x^2 + y^2 preserves monotonic ordering without expensive floating-point square roots.
complexity.notes: Quickselect achieves O(N) average time, while sorting is universally concise and optimal in memory.
